newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Schengen meets on plans to embrace new members.
newsitem.headline: Schengen meets on plans to embrace new members.

text.p: Ministers from the Schengen border-free pact meet in Luxembourg on Thursday in a bid to push forward plans to bring new countries into the alliance.
Luxembourg, currently president of the bloc, wants to advance preparations to admit the five Nordic countries, so they can become signatories by the end of the year, diplomats said.
At stake is full membership for three European Union members Denmark, Sweden and Finland, and associate membership for Norway and Iceland, which are outside the EU.

Seven full members of the zone -- France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Portugal, Spain and Germany -- dropped airport passport checks for each others' nationals on March 26, 1995 when Schengen came into effect.

But the accord, named after the Luxembourg town in which it was signed, quickly fell short of expectations after France, in deep disagreement with the Netherlands over drugs policy, refused to drop land border checks as planned on July 1, 1995.
To this day it maintains checks on its land borders with Belgium and Luxembourg, accusing them of being transit points for Dutch drugs.

Thursday's meeting is expected to concentrate on technical preparations to admit the new countries, which were all admitted as observers in April, rather than persuading France to come fully on board.

Diplomats say details to be ironed out include how the EU's asylum policy and visa policies can be applied to the new members, notably Norway and Iceland, which as non-EU members do not routinely apply the body of EU legislation.
The expansion has financial implications for the group.
Its Schengen Information System computer system -- seen as essential to the common fight against crime -- was, diplomats said, only conceived for five countries.
The computer contains, among other things, lists of people considered undesireable, to help in processing visa applications and preventing illegal immigration in the border-free zone.
The meeting will also take stock of preparations by signatories Austria, Italy and Greece, to become full practising members.
Although they have signed, they have yet to make the final practical preparations to drop their borders. Italy has said it intends to be a full member by March 1997.
The Schengen partners will also, at Spain's request, discuss how to fight terrorism in the bloc.
The rest of the 15-nation EU is eyeing Schengen as a possible model for a border-free zone in the Union as a whole.
The EU has stalled at dropping border checks, fearing it will become a playground for organised crime.
